2. How to Open the Website

Easiest method (recommended): Double-click index.html . It opens directly in your browser and works completely offline. This works because the site uses <script src="..."> tags to load data (not fetch() ), which avoids the CORS restrictions browsers place on file:// pages trying to load JSON. Optional method: If you later add features that need fetch() , run a lightweight local server instead: open a terminal in the study-notes folder and run python -m http.server 8000 , then visit http://localhost:8000 . Not required for the current setup — doubleclicking index.html is sufficient.
3. How to Add New Content
All content lives in js/data.js . Never edit the HTML files to add content.

Add a new chapter Open js/data.js , find the subject (e.g. physics ), and add an object to its chapters array: js { id: "chapter-3", title: "Chapter 3", description: "Short description.", topics: [ { id: "topic-1", title: "Topic 1" } ] }
Add a new topic to an existing chapter Add an object to that chapter's topics array: js { id: "topic-4", title: "Topic 4" }
Add the actual notes for a topic In the same file, find TOPIC_CONTENT and add an entry keyed as "subjectKey__chapterId__topicId" :

js "physics__chapter-1__topic-2": { notes: [ "Content 1 — your first block of notes.", "Content 2 — your second block of notes.", "Content 3 — your third block of notes." ], diagrams: [ { type: "placeholder", label: "Diagram 1", caption: "Describe the diagram h ], examples: [ { title: "Example 1", problem: "...", solution: "..." } ], practice: { mcqs: ["Question text..."], short: [], long: [], numericals: [] }, formulas: [ { name: "Newton's Second Law", expression: "F = ma" } ], keyPoints: ["Key point one.", "Key point two."], summary: "One paragraph wrapping up the topic.",

// 8 optional extra sections shown after Summary — each is just an // array of plain strings, same as keyPoints. Leave any of them out // (or use []) and that section shows a "not added yet" placeholder. specialNotes: ["Special note 1."], importantStatements: ["Important statement 1."], importantNotes: ["Important note 1."], examShortTricks: ["Short trick 1."], examNotes: ["Exam-focused note 1."], quickMcqs: ["MCQ question 1."], importantConcepts: ["Important concept 1."], importantTasks: ["Important task 1."] }

You can add as many notes entries as you want (Content 1, Content 2, Content 3...) — the page automatically numbers and displays each one. Basic HTML is allowed inside any string ( <b> , <i> , <u> , <ul><li> , <table> , <sup> , <sub> , etc.).
Until a topic has a TOPIC_CONTENT entry, its page still works — it shows clean "not added yet" placeholders in every section instead of breaking.
Add a concept diagram (you can add more than one per topic)

In js/data.js , each topic's TOPIC_CONTENT entry has a diagrams array — add as many diagram objects as you want. As soon as a topic has 2+ diagrams, a tab strip appears automatically above the diagram box so the reader can switch between them.
js
diagrams: [ { type: "svg", label: "Diagram 1", caption: "...", svg: `<svg viewBox="0 0 48 { type: "image", label: "Diagram 2", caption: "...", src: "assets/diagrams/yo ]

type: "svg" — paste raw <svg>...</svg> markup into the svg field. Use var(-accent) / var(--card-color) for strokes/fills so it matches light & dark mode automatically. type: "image" — put a PNG/SVG file in assets/diagrams/ and point src at it. label is optional — it's what shows on the tab button when there's more than one diagram.
Every diagram automatically gets zoom in/out, drag-to-pan, fullscreen, and reset controls — you don't need to build those yourself.

Add a new subject Add a new top-level key to STUDY_DATA in js/data.js , following the same shape as physics / chemistry /etc. It will automatically appear as a new home page card, in the sidebar, and in search — no HTML changes needed.
4. Packaging for Distribution
Zip the entire study-notes folder as-is. Anyone can unzip it and double-click index.html — no installation, no dependencies, works on Windows/Mac/Linux, works completely offline.
5. Recommended Access Method

Double-click index.html . This is the simplest and recommended method for this project, since all data loading uses <script> tags rather than fetch() , so there are no CORS issues when opening directly from disk. A local server is only needed if you later add fetch() based features (e.g. loading .json files instead of .js ).
